channel.title: Weekly Worker — Democracy & State (unofficial)
channel.description: Unofficial RSS feed of articles published by Weekly Worker — Democracy & State.

item.title: Challenging false assumptions
item.description: According to the standard Trotskyist narrative, the 1956 events in Hungary were an aborted political revolution. A comforting story that led them to celebrate the restoration of capitalism in eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union over 1989-91. Mike Macnair always had his doubts
item.dc:creator: Mike Macnair

item.title: Managing, not replacing capitalism
item.description: Price controls, buffer stocks and taxing the rich will not get beyond first base while finance, business and resources remain in private hands. Michael Roberts critiques ‘anti-fascist economics’
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts

item.title: Milburn’s recipe for social murder
item.description: Andy Burnham says no one need lose out when it comes to solving the ‘Neets crisis’. But the reality will be conscription into low-paid, dead-end jobs for the benefit of the least competitive sections of the capitalist class. Ian Spencer investigates
item.dc:creator: Ian Spencer

item.title: A long old road
item.description: Nigel with pet dog, Nigel posing as Kitchener, Nigel solving the pothole crisis. Edited by ex-leftist Mick Hume, Reform UK’s new paper has been launched. Paul Demarty reads it, so you don’t have to
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Revolutionary road to democracy
item.description: With the Democrats taking control of both houses of Congress and a much-expanded DSA contingent, it might appear that the US constitution has proven itself fit for socialist purposes. That is far from the case, argues Ian F. America needs a new, democratic, constitution
item.dc:creator: Ian F

item.title: Readying for the next stage
item.description: November 5 sees the trade unions calling a general strike. It will be massive. Till then, argues Jean Laurel, the left needs to keep up the momentum of protests and demonstrations. The left also needs to promote the idea of the organised working class maintaining discipline and good order
item.dc:creator: Jean Laurel

item.title: How to steal an election
item.description: Donald Trump’s Department of Homeland Security is conspiring to throw out millions of mail-in ballots under the guise of ‘election security’. Socialists must defend the right to vote, argues Nick D of the Marxist Unity Group. Socialists must also oppose the undemocratic system which enables the presidential dictatorship
item.dc:creator: Nick D

item.title: Programme for a kingdom
item.description: Among those expelled under the anti-communist proscribed list is Chris Williamson, the former Labour MP and former deputy leader of the Workers Party of Britain. Steve Freeman calls for his reinstatement and an urgent change of course
item.dc:creator: Steve Freeman

item.title: Who we support in Russia
item.description: While it is correct to oppose Nato’s proxy war in Ukraine, we cannot support Russia or ignore the reactionary nature of Putin’s dictatorial regime. Instead, argues Yassamine Mather, we should look to the anti-war left
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Soft left strengthens Vox
item.description: Housing, migration and the prospect of the hard right entering government for the first time since 1975 are the dominant issues, says Paul Davies. But what about the democratic republic, Nato and working class rule?
item.dc:creator: Paul Davies

item.title: Youth take the lead
item.description: High schoolers have blockaded their schools and taken to the streets in unprecedented numbers. They have been joined by university students, teachers and parents. And on November 5 there is the call for a one-day general strike and mass demonstrations. Jean Laurel reports
item.dc:creator: Jean Laurel

item.title: Burnham on the front foot
item.description: With talk of a National Care Service, public ownership and electoral reform, Andy Burnham made the most of his first conference speech as prime minister. But he is not master of his own fate, suggests Paul Demarty
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Cruel and unusual treatment
item.description: Her botched execution is a gruesome reminder of the utterly barbaric nature of the death penalty, says Eddie Ford. But what about dealing with counterrevolutionaries during a bitterly fought civil war?
item.dc:creator: Eddie Ford
